$meta.description: A `file` object can be acquired by either using [File](#COMPUTER_FILE) or [overflow](#METALIB_OVERFLOW). The `classID` used for this object is `"file"`. Game objects compare and hash by identity, and repeated retrieval of the same underlying file returns the same object. Path operations require execute permission on each parent folder.

chmod.description: Changes file permissions and returns an empty `string` on success or an error `string` on failure. A non-number `isRecursive` returns `"chmod: Invalid arguments"`; inaccessible files can return `"permission denied"`.

copy.description: Copies a file or folder and returns one on success. Argument and path validation failures return error strings. If some nested items cannot be copied, returns `"Warning: one or more files or folders cannot be copied."`. Read access is required, including execute permission on every parent folder; SSH encryption still raises.
example: print("There was an error while copying file: " + copyResult)

move.description: Moves a file or folder and returns one on success. Invalid arguments, long names, and oversized paths return error strings instead of raising. The operation requires execute permission on every parent folder; SSH encryption still raises.
example: print("There was an error while moving file: " + moveResult)

symlink.description: Creates a symlink and returns one on success. Invalid arguments, long names, and oversized paths return error strings instead of raising. The operation requires execute permission on every parent folder; SSH encryption still raises.
example: print("There was an error while creating symlink: " + symResult)

rename.description: Rename the file with the name provided. Files can only be renamed if the user has write permissions or is root. The new filename has to be below 128 characters and alphanumeric. On failure, this method will return a `string` with details. Otherwise, this method will return an empty string. If this method is used within an SSH encryption process, an error will be thrown, causing the script execution to be interrupted. In case the provided name is `null`, this method will return a `number` with the value zero.
example: print("There was an error while renaming file: " + renameResult)

path.description: Returns a `string` containing the file path. If the file is a symlink, the optional `symlinkOrigPath` argument can be set to return the original path of the linked file instead. If the file has been deleted, this method will still return the path it had prior to deletion.

is_folder.description: Returns a `number`. The value is one if the file is a folder, zero otherwise. In case the file gets deleted this method will return `null` instead.

parent.description: Returns the parent folder of the current file or folder. In case there is no parent folder `null` will be returned instead. In case the file gets deleted this method will return `null` as well.

name.description: Returns a `string` with the name of the file. In case the file gets deleted this method will return `null` instead.

allow_import.description: Returns a `number`. If the file is binary and can be imported by other scripts, the value will be one; otherwise, the value will be zero. In case the file gets deleted, this method will cause a crash.

get_content.description: Returns a `string` representing the content of the file. To read a file, the user requires read access or being root. Note that you cannot read a binary file. In case of failure, `null` will be returned. If this method is used within an SSH encryption process, an error will be thrown, preventing any further script execution.

set_content.description: Saves text into a `file`. The content will not get appended to the `file`; therefore, existing content will be overridden. To set new content, the user requires write permissions or being root. Keep in mind that text files cannot exceed the character limit of 160,000. In case setting the content was successful, a `number` with the value one will be returned. Otherwise, a `string` with details will be returned. If this method is used within an SSH encryption process, an error will be thrown, preventing any further script execution. If the provided content is `null` or permissions are lacking, this method will return a `number` with the value zero. In case the file gets deleted this method will return `null`.
example: print("There was an error while setting file content: " + setResult)
print("Unable to set content of file!")

is_binary.description: Returns a `number`. If the file is a binary, the value will be one; otherwise, it will be zero. In case the file gets deleted, this method will return `null` instead.

is_symlink.description: Returns a `number`. If the file is a symlink, the value will be one; otherwise, it will be zero. In case the file gets deleted, this method will return `null` instead.

has_permission.description: Returns a `number` indicating if the user who launched the script has the requested permissions. One will indicate that the user has the correct permissions. In case permissions are lacking, the value will be zero. There are three different permission types: read `"r"`, write `"w"`, and execute `"x"`. In case the file gets deleted, this method will return `null` instead.
example: print("Is able to execute ls: " + lsBinary.has_permission("x"))

delete.description: Deletes a file or folder and returns an empty `string` on complete success. Partial deletion returns `"Warning: one or more files or folders cannot be deleted."`; denied access cancels the whole operation with `"Deletion cancelled: permission denied: <path>. No files or folders were deleted."`. Execute permission is required on every parent folder.
example: print("There was an error while deleting a file: " + deletionResult)

get_folders.description: Returns a `list` of child folders. Returns `null` for a missing folder or non-folder object, and `"Permission denied: <path>"` when the folder is unreadable.

get_files.description: Returns a `list` of child files. Returns `null` for a missing folder or non-folder object, and `"Permission denied: <path>"` when the folder is unreadable.

permissions.description:
Returns a `string` with the current file permissions. In case the current file gets deleted, this method will return `null`. The format for this permissions `string` is as follows: `"[fileType][wrx](u)[wrx](g)[wrx](o)"`. The file type is either `"d"` in case it's a directory or `"-"`. The user type gets defined through three possible types: user `"u"`, group `"g"`, and other `"o"`. There are three different permission types: read `"r"`, write `"w"`, and execute `"x"`. An example of a `string` returned by this method would be `"-rwxr-xr-x"`. Taking the latter as an example, the following things become clear:
* The provided file is not a directory.
* The user has full access.
* The group and others have almost all permissions besides writing.

owner.description: Returns a `string` with the name of the file owner. User permissions get applied to whoever is the owner of a file. In case the current file gets deleted, this method will return `null`.

set_owner.description: Changes the file owner and returns an empty `string` on success. Invalid owner values and a non-number recursive flag return error strings instead of raising. Missing files and other signature mismatches return `null`.
example: print("There was an error while changing owner: " + ownerResult)

group.description: Returns a `string` with the name of the group to which this file belongs. Group permissions get applied to whoever is the owner of a file. In case the current file gets deleted, this method will return `null`.
example: print("File is related to following group: " + lsBinary.group)

set_group.description: Changes the file group and returns an empty `string` on success. Invalid group values and a non-number recursive flag return error strings instead of raising. Missing files and other signature mismatches return `null`.
example: print("There was an error while changing group: " + ownerResult)

size.description: Returns a `string` with the size of the file in bytes. There is no correlation between file size and actual file content. Instead, the file size is depending on the name of the file. In case the current file gets deleted, this method will return `null`.
example: print("File size is bigger than 1000 bytes.")

date.description: Returns the file timestamp as `"dd/MMM/yyyy HH:mm"` using invariant English month abbreviations, for example `"05/Mar/2026 14:07"`. Returns `null` if the file no longer exists. Symlinks are not followed and no permission check is performed.
